findings.title: Vocabulary decoration write requires an entry_id before the turn entry exists
findings.location: SPEC-00 §2 Seam G and Seam C; SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5; SPEC-07 §8.2
findings.evidence: SPEC-00: "The agent loop calls `IVocabularyResolver` ... BEFORE constructing tool calls." and "Upon turn completion ... hands it to `DhfLedger.AppendTurnAsync`." SPEC-07: "Stage 5: Durable Decoration Persistence ... Awaits SPEC-04 `DhfDecorationWriter` INSERT" and "The decoration is linked to the agent-turn entry (via `entry_id`)".
findings.problem: The spec requires SPEC-07 to persist a DHF decoration before returning vocabulary success, but the referenced DHF turn entry is only created later at turn completion. No mechanism is defined for obtaining or reserving the `entry_id` at vocabulary-resolution time.
findings.why_it_matters: This is an impossible contract as written. Implementation will either block on an undefined preallocation path or invent hidden coupling between SPEC-05/03/04 that the document never declares.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one explicit mechanism: (a) make SPEC-07 return decoration payload only and persist it after `AppendTurnAsync` returns an `entry_id`, or (b) define a preallocated turn/entry identifier created before vocabulary resolution and carried through the turn lifecycle and DHF append.

findings.title: Entry-detail API breaks the session-capability access model
findings.evidence: The route is `GET /api/dhf/entries/{entryId}` with no `sessionId` requirement, while §5.1 says "the entry ID alone does not grant access; the session sidebar hides entries from other sessions."
findings.problem: The spec defines no access-control check tying entry-detail reads to a presented session capability. Hiding links in the sidebar is not authorization.
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone who obtains an `entryId` can fetch entry content directly, which defeats the stated URL-as-capability boundary based on `sessionId`.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a valid `sessionId` capability on every entry-detail request and verify the requested `entryId` belongs to that session/tenant before returning data. If you want entry-only URLs, sign them with session-scoped capability data instead of relying on obscurity.

findings.title: Acceptance-test IDs ACC-25/26/27 are assigned to different meanings in SPEC-00 and SPEC-07
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 defines ACC-25/26/27 as durable session lock, recovery-context persistence, and neutral landing page. SPEC-07 redefines ACC-25/26/27 as multi-domain resolution, decoration durability/circuit-breaker, and bouncer-cache raw-utterance isolation.
findings.problem: The global acceptance-test namespace is no longer unique.
findings.why_it_matters: Cross-spec traceability and never-descopable gate enforcement become ambiguous. Test reports and review comments cannot reliably refer to ACC-25/26/27 anymore.
findings.proposed_fix: Renumber the SPEC-07 additions to unused ACC IDs and update every cross-reference, including the SPEC-00 master table and any gate lists.

findings.title: SPEC-04 defines incompatible hash inputs in adjacent sections
findings.evidence: §4.2 `DhfHashColumns` includes `"entry_id", "session_id", "sequence_number"`, while §4.2a lists those same columns under "columns NOT included in `DhfHashColumns`".
findings.problem: The hash contract has two conflicting definitions of what is hashed.
findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations of append and validation can compute different `record_hash` values from the same row, which breaks deterministic chain verification.
findings.proposed_fix: Make one hashed-column list authoritative and remove the contradictory exclusions. Add a build-breaking doc/code sync test that compares the documented exclusion table against the actual `DhfHashColumns` set.

findings.title: Locked same-AddinSessionId sessions on other workstations are ignored during session open
findings.evidence: The first lookup only considers rows with `ended_at IS NULL AND locked_at IS NULL`. The second lookup for locked rows adds `AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId`.
findings.problem: A locked open session with the same tenant+`addin_session_id` on a different workstation matches neither branch, so a new session can be inserted with the same AddinSessionId.
findings.why_it_matters: This bypasses SDR-04-008's hard-error rule for cross-workstation collisions and allows duplicate epochs for the same tenant to coexist.
findings.proposed_fix: Before inserting, query for any open row with the same tenant+AddinSessionId regardless of lock state. If workstation differs, throw `CrossWorkstationSessionConflictException`; if workstation matches and the row is locked, throw `SessionLockedException`.

findings.title: Planned disconnect escalation can terminate SolidWorks and lose unrelated unsaved work
findings.evidence: `Environment.Exit(1)` is specified, and the document states this "terminates the SolidWorks process" and that "unsaved work in other open documents may be lost."
findings.problem: A stuck add-in call during disconnect escalates to killing the host CAD process, not just failing the add-in session.
findings.why_it_matters: This turns an add-in fault into host-wide data loss and makes a routine disconnect/shutdown path unsafe.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `Environment.Exit(1)` from in-process add-in paths. Leave the add-in in a failed state, surface a hard error requiring manual SolidWorks shutdown, or move any forced termination behavior into an external watchdog process that is not the CAD host.

top_3_must_fix: Define a valid mechanism for associating vocabulary-resolution decorations with a DHF entry before persistence, or move decoration persistence until after the turn entry exists.
Resolve the SPEC-04 hash-contract contradiction so append and validation use the same hashed-column set.
Remove `Environment.Exit(1)` from the add-in disconnect escalation path to avoid host-process termination and data loss.
